web_blocks.html: AJMERA's tape shifted sharply in late November 2026, breaking out of its 11.7% Bollinger squeeze into an extended Stage 2 markup [26][27]. Reconciling the 2026-11-23 NSE ledger with the 2026-11-25 live TradingView snapshot clarifies the risk [26][27]. On the 2026-11-23 ledger, shares jumped +8.93% to ₹162.62 (+22.76% 1W, +36.58% 3M) on 28.03 million shares—28.44x average volume [27]. That surge upgraded the ledger to Stage 2 (Markup), pushing 63D RS to +31.96% (28D RS +25.74%) and daily RSI to 78.26 [27]. On November 24, Company Secretary Reema Solanki filed a voluntary Reg 30 note on the Nov 20 and Nov 23 volume spikes [34]. She confirmed zero undisclosed news (UPSI) and invited exchange surveillance review if appropriate [34].

Two days later, the 2026-11-25 live TradingView snapshot prints ₹160.92 (-1.05% 1D, +19.20% 1W, +30.62% 1M, -17.22% 1Y) on 2.59 million shares (1.45x avg volume) [26]. Price cleared both Pivot R1 (₹143.85) and Pivot R2 (₹155.11), flipping in_thewrap_stage2 to True (RS 82.1; sector density 35.7%, rank 35) [26]. Yet the tape is stretched far past actionable zones. Shares sit +18.25% above the 10W EMA (₹136.09), +26.90% above the 50D SMA (₹126.81), and +27.01% above the 30W SMA (₹126.70) [26]. Momentum is overbought across timeframes: 4H RSI is 78.69, Daily RSI is 76.31, and Weekly RSI is 69.58 [26]. Bollinger Band width doubled to 22.88% while ATR(14) climbed to ₹8.19 (5.09% of price) [26]. TradingView enforces WAIT_FOR_SUPPORT_PULLBACK and CAP_WAIT_FOR_SUPPORT (support ₹134.05–₹140.37, TV stop ₹122.61), while our negative valuation skew (-7.4% E[P] to ₹149.00) pushes new capital all the way to REJECTED [26].

web_blocks.html: 4-Hour Exhaustion, Unexplained Volume & Derivatives Constraint: On the 4-hour chart, 4H RSI hit 78.69. Price sits nearly ₹18 above its 4H EMA20 (₹143.04) and ₹27 above its 4H SMA50 (₹134.22) [26]. Promoters hold 68.56% (0.02% pledge), while DII/FII ownership stays below 2% [8][43]. A 28.03-million-share day (~45% of public float) with zero undisclosed news signals HNI momentum rotation, not steady fund buying [27][34]. Because AJMERA has no NSE F&O chain (NOT_OPTIONABLE_OR_ILLIQUID), we cannot sell calls into this 76.31 RSI spike [28]. Trimming 50% of our cash equity and ratcheting the stop to ₹134.00 is our cleanest forward risk control.

Tightened Upward-Only Stop-Loss Ratchet (₹117.00 → ₹134.00): Evaluated strictly on forward mark-to-market risk from ₹160.92, leaving a stop at ₹117.00 (-27.3%) or even ₹125.00 (-22.3%) exposes too much live equity on an overvalued cyclical [26]. Meanwhile, the rising 10-week EMA has climbed to ₹136.09, right alongside the 20-day SMA (₹137.08) and TradingView's ₹134.05 support floor [26]. Ratcheting our hard weekly-close stop upward by +₹17.00 to ₹134.00 sits cleanly beneath the 10-week EMA, tightening residual mark-to-market downside on the remaining 650 shares to -16.7% while still giving the Stage 2 trend room to breathe.

web_blocks.title: Why We Reject New Capital Yet Retain 650 Shares Behind a ₹134.00 Stop
paragraphs: 1. Zero Fresh Capital Into Negative Expected Value: With Base fair value at ₹148.00 and E[P] at ₹149.00 (-7.4% vs. ₹160.92), even a pullback to ₹134–₹140 fails our 1.50:1 asymmetry hurdle, enforcing REJECTED (TIER_0) [26].

2. Disciplined Trend Participation on Half Size: Cutting exposure from 4.96% to ~2.45% NAV (650 shares) and tightening the weekly stop to ₹134.00 (below 10W EMA ₹136.09) respects Stage 2 momentum without over-allocating live capital [26].

book_paragraphs: Turning from valuation to the tape, Ajmera Realty just delivered the kind of explosive technical breakout that tests every ounce of an investor's discipline. Just eight trading days ago, the stock was quietly coiling inside an 11.7% Bollinger Band squeeze near ₹132 to ₹136, still stuck in Stage 3 on our deterministic ledger. Today, that coil has detonated upward—transforming Ajmera into a confirmed Stage 2 markup on both the November 23 NSE ledger and the November 25 live TradingView snapshot.

Look closely at the exact numbers across both cutoffs so we never confuse momentum excitement with low-risk entry. On the verified November 23 NSE ledger, Ajmera jumped 8.93% in a single day to close at ₹162.62—up 22.76% in one week and 36.58% over three months—on an astonishing 28.03 million shares, or 28.44 times its 20-day average volume. That burst formally flipped our ledger classifier to Stage 2 Markup, rocketed 63-day relative strength to +31.96%, and drove daily RSI to 78.26. The volume explosion was so unusual that on November 24, Company Secretary Reema Solanki filed a voluntary Regulation 30 clarification with BSE and NSE confirming that no undisclosed price-sensitive information existed and inviting exchange surveillance review if appropriate.

By the November 25 live TradingView snapshot, shares settled slightly to ₹160.92—down 1.05% on the day on 2.59 million shares (1.45x 30-day average volume)—having cleared both Pivot R1 at ₹143.85 and Pivot R2 at ₹155.11. Ajmera now registers as True on TheWrap Stage 2 with an 82.1 relative-strength percentile. Yet look at the stretch beneath the surface: price sits 18.25% above its 10-week EMA at ₹136.09, 26.90% above its 50-day SMA at ₹126.81, and 27.01% above its 30-week SMA at ₹126.70. Four-hour RSI stands at 78.69, daily RSI at 76.31, and weekly RSI at 69.58, while Bollinger Band width has doubled from 11.7% to 22.88%.

When you combine that +26.9% 50-day extension and unexplained volume burst with Chapter 7's negative expected value (-7.4% to ₹149.00 E[P]), the technical and fundamental messages align completely. New capital is REJECTED (TIER_0), while existing capital trims 50% immediately into strength and ratchets its trailing weekly-close stop up to ₹134.00—just below the rising 10-week EMA.

book_subsections.title: Multi-Timeframe Anatomy: From Overbought 4H Candles to the 10-Week EMA Floor
paragraphs: Walk down the timeframes from weekly to 4-hour and you can see the exact battleground forming beneath ₹160.92. On the 4-hour chart, RSI at 78.69 leaves price nearly ₹18 stretched above its 4H EMA20 at ₹143.04 and ₹27 above its 4H SMA50 at ₹134.22. On the daily chart, daily Average True Range has expanded from ₹6.34 to ₹8.19 on TradingView (₹8.40 on the ledger), meaning routine daily swings now exceed 5% of the share price. Price sits 4.39 ATRs above its 50-day moving average—a classic mean-reversion rubber band.

On the downside, the first decisive trend floor sits right at the rising 10-week EMA (₹136.09), reinforced by the 20-day SMA (₹137.08), the 4-hour 50-period SMA (₹134.22), and TradingView's ₹134.05 support lower bound. Setting our ratcheted hard weekly-close stop at ₹134.00—an upward move of +₹17.00 from our prior ₹117.00 floor and +₹11.39 above TradingView's ₹122.61 base stop—directly protects the Stage 2 trend without waiting for a full -22% to -27% collapse back to the 50-day and 200-day moving averages (₹125.21–₹126.81).

On the upside, having cleared Pivot R1 (₹143.85) and Pivot R2 (₹155.11), the next major pocket of trapped supply from the 2025–2026 cycle sits near our ₹195.00 Bull target and the ₹205.98–₹208.96 52-week high. Keeping half of our Zerodha stake (650 shares, ~2.45% NAV) behind a ₹134.00 weekly stop lets us participate if momentum carries higher, while refusing to risk a full 4.96% weight on an unconfirmed volume spike.

book_subsections.title: Float Forensics: What a 28.44x Volume Explosion Actually Means
paragraphs: Understanding Ajmera's shareholding structure is essential to interpreting November 23's 28.03-million-share frenzy. As of September 2026, promoters hold 68.56% of the company with a negligible 0.02% share pledge, leaving a public float of 31.44%—and combined DII and FII ownership sits below 2%. Following the January 2026 1:5 equity share split (face value ₹10 to ₹2), daily liquidity improved, with 30-day average volume hovering near 1.79 million shares.

When 28.03 million shares change hands in a single session—nearly half the entire non-promoter float—without a single corporate press release, earnings beat, or land-conversion order, institutional tape readers immediately shift from accumulation mode to capital-preservation mode. Management's proactive November 24 Regulation 30 clarification was good governance, reassuring investors that no unannounced corporate event was leaking. Yet from a market-structure standpoint, it also confirms that this +22.8% weekly surge was driven by momentum chasing, algorithmic breakouts, or HNI block rotation rather than verified H2 FY27 pre-sales.

Historically in Indian mid-cap real estate, unexplained 20x+ volume spikes above 75 RSI resolve in one of two ways: either a constructive 3-to-6-week flag consolidation back toward the rising 10-week EMA (₹136.09) as volume dries up, or a painful round-trip back to the 50-day moving average (₹126.81). In neither scenario does chasing ₹160.92 with fresh capital—or holding an oversized 4.96% weight—offer favorable forward odds.

book_subsections.title: Navigating Narrow Breadth and Cash-Equity-Only Constraints
paragraphs: Macro context reinforces this caution. On the November 23 ledger, the Nifty 50 remains in an Uptrend characterized by narrow breadth: just 55.2% of the 500-stock breadth pool sits above its 50-day moving average and only 48.2% above its 200-day moving average, with three distribution days logged over the past twenty-five sessions. Meanwhile, Real Estate Development carries a modest 35.7% Stage 2 sector density (rank 35). In narrow-breadth markets, extended mid-cap breakouts frequently suffer abrupt 15%–20% air pockets whenever index volatility ticks up.

Add to that the derivatives constraint: Ajmera Realty is not permitted in the NSE Futures and Options segment (NOT_OPTIONABLE_OR_ILLIQUID). In Tier-1 peers like Lodha or Oberoi Realty, a desk holding an extended stock at 76 RSI could sell out-of-the-money calls to collect volatility premium and cushion a pullback. In Ajmera, your only two risk-management levers are harvesting cash equity into strength and ratcheting your hard stop-loss upward.

That is why our technical plan is so decisive. First, we reject new capital outright (REJECTED, TIER_0) rather than trying to catch a falling knife at ₹134–₹140 when Base fair value sits at ₹148.00. Second, we use the ₹160.92 liquidity window to trim 650 of our 1,300 held shares (50%), harvesting ~₹1,04,598 cash while volume is elevated. Third, we ratchet our hard weekly-close stop upward from ₹117.00 to ₹134.00 on the remaining 650 shares, capping forward mark-to-market downside at -16.7%.

book_subsections.title: Clear Invalidation vs. Stage 2 Continuation Gates
paragraphs: Every open position needs bright, non-negotiable guardrails. On the downside, ₹134.00 on a weekly closing basis is our new line in the sand—ratcheted ₹17.00 above our prior ₹117.00 stop and sitting right below the rising 10-week EMA (₹136.09) and 4H SMA50 (₹134.22). A weekly close under ₹134.00 would mean the November breakout shelf has failed, triggering an immediate exit of the remaining 650 shares.

On the upside, constructive Stage 2 continuation requires two developments: first, a controlled, low-volume consolidation that lets daily RSI cool from 76.31 back toward 50–55 while price holds above the ₹136.09 10-week EMA; and second, fundamental validation from Q3–Q4 FY27 pre-sales showing that Ajmera is genuinely closing its ₹1,893 crore H2 launch hurdle. Pay close attention to how the weekly moving-average ribbon behaves after a vertical spike like November 23. Right now, the 10-week EMA sits at ₹136.09 and the 30-week SMA sits at ₹126.70—creating an unusually wide ₹24 to ₹34 gap beneath the ₹160.92 live print. Watching whether volume dries up below 1.0 million shares per day above ₹134.00 will tell us quickly whether the remaining 650 shares deserve to stay open toward ₹195.00 or exit cleanly on stop.

Notice how clean this dual-layer technical discipline is from a portfolio-construction perspective. By cutting 650 shares immediately at ₹160.92, we remove ₹1,04,598 of live capital from an overbought 76.31 RSI spike and eliminate any temptation to rationalize a 27% drawdown back to ₹117.00. On the remaining 650 shares (~2.45% NAV), ratcheting the weekly-close stop up to ₹134.00 directly beneath the rising 10-week EMA enforces strict forward risk control: if the breakout holds above trend support and momentum extends toward ₹195.00, we participate meaningfully; if the unexplained volume spike fades and breaks ₹134.00, we exit automatically with forward mark-to-market risk capped at -16.7%.
